documentation: Unseeded Random / Random.Default calls compile to plain math.random with no helper code. Random(seed) is a port of Kotlin's XorWow generator (src/main/resources/runtime/random.lua), so every seeded Random is independent and produces the same sequence as the JVM.

declarations.name: Random
declarations.documentation: Random.Default / Random → math.random; Random(seed: Int) → an independent seeded XorWow generator matching Kotlin. A Long seed is not supported

declarations.name: nextInt
declarations.documentation: Full Int range; seeded instances match Kotlin bit for bit. Also accepts a range argument, nextInt(1..6)

declarations.name: nextInt
declarations.documentation: from inclusive, until exclusive; also covers nextInt(until). Also accepts a range argument, nextInt(1..6)

declarations.name: nextDouble
declarations.documentation: [0, 1); also covers nextDouble(until) and nextDouble(from, until)

declarations.name: asJavaRandom
declarations.documentation: Identity: there is only one Random type

declarations.name: asKotlinRandom
declarations.documentation: Identity: there is only one Random type

declarations.name: nextLong
declarations.documentation: Direct math.random; the no-argument form spans +-2^52 because Lua numbers are doubles. Also accepts nextLong(until), nextLong(from, until) and a range argument

declarations.name: nextUBytes
declarations.documentation: A Lua array of random bytes (used as a List); a seeded Random matches the JVM sequence

declarations.name: nextUInt
declarations.documentation: Direct math.random; a seeded Random matches the JVM sequence. Also accepts nextUInt(until), nextUInt(from, until) and a range argument

declarations.name: nextULong
declarations.documentation: Direct math.random; the no-argument form spans 0..2^53 because Lua numbers are doubles. Also accepts nextULong(until), nextULong(from, until) and a range argument
